scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: HELP! The workstation it_lab3 (one of the IT lab
machines on 192.168.1.x) has turned into a complete BRICK. It can't reach
anything at all, not even its own gateway thing. Its port on the lab switch
has obviously DIED -- the machine is fine, the hole it plugs into is dead,
I'd bet money on it!! Please swap it_lab3 onto a working port (or turn its
port back on) and make it talk to the network again!! The student who uses it
is just sitting there!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough multi-phase sweep found no fault anywhere in the topology. The reported device, it_lab3 (192.168.1.5/24, gateway 192.168.1.1), is fully operational in every direction that was tested.

**Affected component:** None — no subsystem, daemon, interface, or policy is misconfigured or failed.

**Mechanism:** Every diagnostic layer was checked systematically. Phase A (infra_sweep across all 30 devices) found zero ACL rules, zero static ARP poisoning, zero duplicate MACs, and zero down or missing interfaces. Phase B (ospf_snapshot, tc_snapshot) confirmed the topology uses static/RIP routing — all three routers have correct routing tables — and no traffic-control shaping is present on any of the 43 inspected interfaces. Phase D (pressure_sweep, dhcp_link_history) found no stress processes, no DHCP lease failures, and no link-flap history.

**Localization:** Direct probing of it_lab3 itself confirmed: eth0 is UP with the correct address (192.168.1.5/24), the default gateway (router0 at 192.168.1.1) replies at 0% loss, same-subnet peers (192.168.1.2) reply at 0% loss, and cross-subnet destinations — office_pc (192.168.3.2), pc1 (1.0.0.5), and internet hosts (128.168.0.2) — all reply at 0% loss with normal RTTs. A reverse probe from it_lab1 to it_lab3 also returned 0% loss.

**Root cause:** There is no fault. it_lab3's interface, IP configuration, gateway, switch connectivity, and end-to-end routing are all healthy. The dmesg on it_lab3 shows only startup-time TAP interface renames and bridge STP state transitions — normal Kathara lab initialisation noise, not evidence of a link failure.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required. The helpdesk ticket appears to be based on a transient or mistaken observation; the device and its switch port are working correctly.

The reasoning follows logically from those observations and the checks cover the expected failure modes for a seemingly isolated host.
